evidence: _require_write_auth is defined at server.py:274 in build_server's body; import_memory (404) is nested in the if cfg.memory.allow_import branch (392) of the same function, so it is in closure scope and called at 411. It raises RuntimeError (281). The same file's other tools (e.g. import_memory itself at 415, 424) already raise RuntimeError; FastMCP's tool manager wraps exceptions from tool functions in ToolError and the low-level MCP server returns them as CallToolResult isError=true. I did not read the installed mcp package source, so that wrapping rests on known library behaviour.

server.py:411 calls _require_write_auth("memory") as the first statement of import_memory, before parse_json (413) and import_bundle (418). The gate (server.py:280) raises RuntimeError iff cfg.auth.mode == "none" and not cfg.auth.insecure. config.py:235 mode is Literal["none","bearer","jwt"], so bearer and jwt pass the gate (jwt is also rejected at config validation, config.py:262). The tool is registered once and uses the shared cfg, so the check is transport-independent. The store is only constructed at registration (396), not on a call.

config.py:177-178 says calls require auth.mode='bearer' or auth.insecure=true. AuthConfig.mode is Literal['none','bearer','jwt'] (config.py:235). The gate at server.py:280 raises only when mode=='none' and not insecure, so mode='jwt' also passes. The bearer-only wording is therefore false: jwt is accepted. The same wording appears in the error string at server.py:283.

server.py:411 calls _require_write_auth('memory') before parse_json (413) and import_bundle (418). The gate (274-285) raises RuntimeError when cfg.auth.mode=='none' and not cfg.auth.insecure. _AuthMiddleware (http.py:336-363) calls the authenticator on every HTTP request; BearerTokenAuthenticator (auth/bearer.py:41-47) accepts a request whose Authorization: Bearer <token> matches, with no other credential needed. conftest build_asgi_app(cfg) wires this with the auth config, and the test passes the header on streamablehttp_client for initialize and call_tool (test_memory_import_auth.py:35-41). The gate (server.py:274-285) raises RuntimeError with 'disabled on an unauthenticated endpoint', which FastMCP wraps as a tool error: HTTP 200 with a result whose isError is true and whose text content holds the message. The test asserts result.isError and that text (lines 43-50). Note that the refused cases in the test use mode none, not bearer; the claim's wording is loose on that, but the properties it states hold.

server.py:280-285 raises RuntimeError whose f-string 'is disabled on an ' + 'unauthenticated endpoint. ...' concatenates to contiguous 'disabled on an unauthenticated endpoint'. import_memory calls _require_write_auth('memory') at server.py:411 before parse/import. FastMCP wraps tool exceptions as an isError result with text including the original message, so the substring check on joined text content holds.

tests/unit/_config_builders.py:34 declares `auth: AuthConfig | None = None` (used at :53). AuthConfig (src/sqllens/config.py:230-301): bearer mode validator requires non-empty stripped token with len >= MIN_BEARER_TOKEN_LENGTH (=32, config.py:699). Token 'test-token-01234567890123456789012' is 11+23=34 chars, passes; no other validator rejects bearer+token. mode='none', insecure=True with no token passes all validators (jwt rejected only for jwt mode; token check only if token set).
